chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:
If she was menstruating, then [the waiting period is] one menstruation, and if she was not menstruating, then [the waiting period is] a month and a half.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a woman in temporary marriage (Mut'a) according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the Iddah for Mut'a is determined by the occurrence of menstruation: one cycle if she menstruates, or a fixed period of three months (often interpreted as 45 days or two months in various juristic readings of 'month and a half') if she does not. This ruling distinguishes Mut'a from permanent marriage, where the Iddah is typically three menstrual cycles or three lunar months, highlighting the flexibility of temporary marriage contracts in Shia jurisprudence. The narration underscores the practical application of biological markers in determining legal waiting periods for contract dissolution.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umyer, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘If she was menstruating, so one menstruation, and if she was not menstruating, so a month and a half (as a waiting period)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Waiting period in al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage) is one cycle of Hayd (menses) if she experiences Hayd (menses); and if she does not experience Hayd (menses) then it is one and a half month.’”
